outline: Cartilage growth and extracellular matrix signaling
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Hereditary multiple osteochondromas due to EXT1 loss of function
mechanism: EXT1 and EXT2 form a heparan-sulfate polymerase complex. Loss of EXT function impairs heparan-sulfate chain synthesis and perturbs signaling in growth-plate chondrocytes, predisposing to multiple cartilage-capped osteochondromas.
vignette: A 13-year-old boy has multiple painless bony masses near the knees and wrists that have enlarged during growth. Radiographs show several cartilage-capped exophytic lesions arising from the metaphyses of long bones. His father had similar lesions. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous loss-of-function variant in EXT1.
lead: Which of the following biosynthetic processes is most directly impaired by this mutation?
distractors: Hydroxylation of lysine residues in type I collagen
Addition of mannose-6-phosphate tags to lysosomal hydrolases
Gamma-carboxylation of glutamate residues in osteocalcin
Proteolytic degradation of type I collagen by osteoclast cathepsin K
distractor_notes: Defective lysyl hydroxylation is associated with selected collagen disorders such as PLOD1-related Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, not EXT1-related osteochondromas.
Mannose-6-phosphate targeting defects cause mucolipidosis II/III rather than hereditary multiple osteochondromas.
Vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation is not the molecular function of EXT1/EXT2.
Cathepsin K functions in osteoclast matrix degradation; its loss causes pycnodysostosis rather than EXT-related osteochondromas.
key_expl: EXT1 and EXT2 encode glycosyltransferases that form a heparan-sulfate polymerase complex. Pathogenic loss-of-function variants reduce normal heparan-sulfate synthesis and disturb growth-plate signaling, producing autosomal dominant hereditary multiple osteochondromas.
objective: Identify impaired heparan-sulfate polymerization as the core molecular defect in EXT1/EXT2-related hereditary multiple osteochondromas.
